Agent Receipts Audit · arcs-v9 README.md

The README, Read Cold

A cold reader can say roughly what ARCS does but cannot run it, and four of the README's claims are wrong. Fix 1 puts one plain line, one checkable proof and a working way to try it on the first screen.

Fix 1 · rewriteOpen with one plain line of what ARCS is, one proof a reader can run (the 17 Y-gate tests), and the live compass link that needs no account.

What a reader with no memory of the work could learn from README.md and the paths it names, checked claim by claim against the code. Built from one 48-line README, the paths it names, and two live pages, with no transcript. See all five fixes.

How far a reader with no memory got

Each section carries a support score: how well the repo history backs the claim, not how well it reads. A section that reads well but is thinly backed scores low on purpose. Bands: well grounded (75 to 100) · partial, record is thin (45 to 74) · described, not confirmed (under 45). The weakest section is open; open any other for its evidence.

01 · What ARCS isA question goes in, a bearing comes out, recorded as a receipt.+support 80% · well grounded
What the repo history shows
POST /api/compass makes one Claude call and writes a Receipt row (src/app/api/compass/route.ts lines 355 and 539). Anonymous callers are allowed under ADR-016, rate limited to 10 a minute.
What it does not show
Plain meanings for bearing, terrain, DEWY and Y-gate. The cold reader could not decode them.
What would raise the score
One plain sentence first, and every term expanded on first use.
evidence: src/app/api/compass/route.ts, _DECISIONS/ADR-016-arcs-v9-auth-model.md
02 · How it worksDEWY and the Y-gate are real code; the stage list, the state list and the Observatory replay are described more strongly than they run.+support 55% · partial
What the repo history shows
src/lib/ygate.ts sets six states (GREEN, YELLOW, FORK, PARADOX, DELTA, SCRATCH), and tests/unit/ygate.test.ts runs 17 tests, all passing. The DEWY receipt schema is in runtime/specs.
What it does not show
Six separate stages: L0 to L5 is one Claude call with a staged prompt, and its L3 is a premise check, not a cascade. RED is a warning level that becomes DELTA, not a state. The Observatory replays a fixed dataset about the build, not a user's decision.
What would raise the score
Describe the pipeline as one call with a staged prompt, and the Observatory as a demo of the build's own history.
evidence: src/lib/ygate.ts, tests/unit/ygate.test.ts, runtime/specs/dewy-receipt-schema-v1.json, src/app/observatory/page.tsx
03 · Run itThe Python CLI exists and uses only the standard library, but the README gives no input to feed it and no way to start the web app.+support 35% · described, not confirmed
What the repo history shows
scripts/arcs_cli.py has the six verbs and imports only stdlib modules. scripts/score_me.py runs with no arguments.
What it does not show
A sample input. Run from the repo root, the example *.json picks up package.json and tsconfig.json. No npm install, env vars or database step for the web app.
What would raise the score
Lead with the web app (live link plus local setup from package.json and src/lib/env.ts) and a test command that passes, and mark the CLI as needing scan files.
evidence: scripts/arcs_cli.py, scripts/score_me.py, package.json, src/lib/env.ts
04 · StackNext.js 16, Prisma 7, Auth.js v5 and the Anthropic SDK are right; SQLite in development is not.+support 60% · partial
What the repo history shows
package.json lists each, and globals.css is the one stylesheet.
What it does not show
SQLite anywhere. prisma.config.ts says there is no SQLite fallback, and src/lib/db.ts throws if DATABASE_URL is unset.
What would raise the score
Say Postgres in every environment, and list DATABASE_URL in setup.
evidence: package.json, prisma.config.ts, src/lib/db.ts
05 · Repo topologyFour of six rows point the right way; two are wrong.+support 50% · partial
What the repo history shows
src/app, src/lib/ygate.ts, _DECISIONS (93 files) and runtime/specs hold what the table says.
What it does not show
WORLD.md in _CANON (it is at the root). A 34-file operator library (46 top-level .py files), presented as the live pipeline although its own README says it is not wired in.

evidence: WORLD.md, operators/README.md, _DECISIONS/
06 · Livearcs.care and app.arcs.care both load.+support 90% · well grounded
What the repo history shows
Both return HTTP 200. The app's compass opens at /dashboard with no account, and an example brief is linked from the home page.

evidence: https://app.arcs.care, https://arcs.care

Claims not verified

Not verified means the repo history does not show it. It does not mean it is false. A red light marks a gap a fix below makes checkable.

Gaps in the repo history

  • path wrong
    The repo topology says WORLD.md lives in _CANON/.
    _CANON/WORLD.md does not exist; WORLD.md is at the repo root.
  • stack wrong
    The stack uses SQLite in development and Postgres in production.
    prisma.config.ts says there is no SQLite fallback; both environments use Postgres.
  • count stale
    operators/ is a 34-file Python library.
    operators/ has 46 top-level .py files today; the 34 comes from its own README, also stale.
  • overclaim
    operators/ holds L0-L5 as atomic components.
    operators/README.md says it is not wired into the live compass route or any deployed surface.
  • demo described as product
    The Observatory replays any decision as a kinematic trajectory.
    src/app/observatory/page.tsx renders a fixed dataset about the build's own history; no code path loads a user's receipt into it.
  • pipeline described loosely
    The pipeline runs six stages, signal to global.
    The compass route makes one Claude call; the stages are sections of its prompt.
  • gate count partial
    The Y-gate is a 12D manifold.
    src/lib/ygate.ts numbers 10 checks (1 to 6, 8, 9, 10, 12); 7 and 11 are absent.
  • state list wrong
    The Y-gate states include RED.
    src/lib/ygate.ts uses RED as a warning level and maps it to DELTA; the states it sets are GREEN, YELLOW, FORK, PARADOX, DELTA and SCRATCH.
  • no sample input
    The CLI examples run the full five-verb pipeline.
    They need scan JSON files the repo does not ship; *.json at the root matches config files.
  • toy described as forensic
    score_me.py produces a single-contact forensic receipt.
    It applies fixed constants to a name, title, company and year, reads no data, and prints a link to the private repo.
  • setup missing
    A reader can run the web app from the README.
    No install, env var, database or dev-server step is given; they exist in package.json and src/lib/env.ts.
  • universal claim
    Every architectural decision has a receipt.
    93 ADR files exist; whether every decision got one cannot be checked from the record.

Limits of this run

One cold reader and no paid calls. A rerun with a human reader and one compass call would check both; these are limits of this run, not gaps in the README.

  • one cold reader
    A cold reader reaches the stated understanding.
    One agent (Sonnet) given only the README, plus the auditor's checks. Not a human panel.
  • no paid calls
    The compass returns a bearing for a real question.
    Not exercised: a compass call spends API tokens. The live checks were HTTP status and page text.

Leak map

Paths and features the README named that a reader could not find as described. This is a pointer gap, not a grade.

  • not surfaced _CANON/WORLD.md (the file is at the repo root)
  • not surfaced operators/ as the L0-L5 pipeline (its own README says it is not wired into the live compass)
  • not surfaced the Observatory replaying any decision (src/app/observatory/page.tsx holds a fixed dataset about the build itself)
  • not surfaced SQLite in development (prisma.config.ts and src/lib/db.ts use Postgres in every environment)

Five fixes, ranked

Ranked by the auditor from the gaps above. Each names the gap it closes.

  1. Open with one plain line of what ARCS is, one proof a reader can run (the 17 Y-gate tests), and the live compass link that needs no account. rewrite · closes: setup missing, pipeline described loosely
  2. Correct the four wrong claims: the WORLD.md path, SQLite in development, operators as a reference library with no count, the Observatory as a demo of the build's own history. edit · closes: path wrong, stack wrong, count stale, overclaim, demo described as product
  3. Add local web-app setup taken from package.json and src/lib/env.ts: install, env vars, database, dev server. edit · closes: setup missing
  4. Describe the gate as the checks and states it really has, not a 12D manifold with RED, and say the CLI needs scan files the repo does not ship. edit · closes: gate count partial, state list wrong, no sample input
  5. Replace universal words like every with counts, and label score_me.py as a demo. edit · closes: universal claim, toy described as forensic

What this audit cannot see

  • It reads only the README and what it names. The agent-facing files were out of scope on purpose.
  • It is not a code review. It checks whether each README claim points at something real.
  • It never rates people. It reads the record, not the team.
